pois.name: Grand Turk Cruise Center
pois.description: The cruise ship terminal at the south-west of the island, with shops, the beach and the pier. Return to Ship routes you here - allow plenty of time before all-aboard.
pois.accessNotes: Return-to-ship endpoint is PROVISIONAL until the approved terminal approach point is confirmed (OD-02).

pois.name: Governor's Beach
pois.description: A wide white-sand beach with clear turquoise water and shade trees, popular for swimming and relaxing. One of the closest beaches to the Cruise Center.
pois.facts: The beach takes its name from Waterloo, the Governor’s residence close by.

pois.name: Guanahani Beach (Pillory Beach)
pois.notRoutableReason: No walkable road or path within 250 m (e.g. offshore or no public access)
pois.description: A calm white-sand beach north of Cockburn Town, officially renamed Guanahani Beach in 1992. Good snorkelling close to shore.
pois.facts: Guanahani was the Taíno name for the island where Columbus first landed in 1492.
pois.accessNotes: Access: the small parking area at the north end of Front Street (source: visittci.com).

pois.name: Osprey Beach
pois.notRoutableReason: Location not yet verified on the map data
pois.description: A small beach along the Cockburn Town waterfront, beside historic Front Street.

pois.name: Boaby Rock Beach
pois.notRoutableReason: Location not yet verified on the map data
pois.description: A quieter beach on the south-east of the island with rocky outcrops and open views.

pois.name: White Sands Beach
pois.notRoutableReason: Location not yet verified on the map data
pois.description: A secluded stretch of sand at the southern end of Grand Turk.

pois.name: Cockburn Town
pois.description: The capital of the Turks and Caicos Islands, with colonial-era buildings, churches and the waterfront along Front Street and Duke Street.
pois.facts: Cockburn Town is the capital of the Turks and Caicos Islands.

pois.name: Lighthouse
pois.description: The historic cast-iron lighthouse at the island's northern tip, overlooking the reef and the Atlantic.
pois.facts: The lighthouse was built in 1852 from cast-iron sections made in England, to warn ships away from the reefs off the northern tip.

pois.name: Front Street
pois.notRoutableReason: Location not yet verified on the map data
pois.description: The historic waterfront street of Cockburn Town, lined with old Bermudian-style buildings.
pois.facts: Many buildings on Front Street date from the Bermudian salt-raking era.

pois.name: Turks and Caicos National Museum
pois.notRoutableReason: Location not yet verified on the map data
pois.description: The national museum on Front Street, covering the islands' natural and cultural history.
pois.facts: The museum displays the Molasses Reef wreck, one of the oldest European shipwrecks found in the Americas.

pois.name: H.M. Prison Museum
pois.notRoutableReason: Location not yet verified on the map data
pois.description: The 19th-century Her Majesty’s Prison, now a museum where visitors can see the old cells and courtyard.

pois.notRoutableReason: Location not yet verified on the map data
pois.description: St. Mary’s Anglican Pro-Cathedral, a historic church on the Cockburn Town waterfront.

pois.name: St. Thomas Anglican Church

pois.description: One of the oldest church sites on Grand Turk, north of the town centre.

pois.name: Columbus Landfall National Park
pois.notRoutableReason: Location not yet verified on the map data
pois.description: A protected marine park along the west coast, commemorating one of the proposed landfall sites of Columbus in 1492.
pois.facts: Grand Turk is one of the islands proposed as Christopher Columbus’s first landfall in 1492.

pois.facts: Waterloo has served as the official residence of the Governor of the Turks and Caicos Islands.

pois.name: Town Salina
pois.description: A historic salt pond behind Cockburn Town, a reminder of the island's salt-raking past and a place to spot wading birds.
pois.facts: Salt was raked from Grand Turk’s salinas for centuries, and was once the island’s main export.

pois.name: John Glenn Splashdown Exhibit
pois.description: An exhibit at the Cruise Center about NASA’s Mercury programme and John Glenn’s Friendship 7 flight.
pois.facts: After the first American orbital flight in February 1962, John Glenn’s Friendship 7 capsule splashed down near Grand Turk.
